scorecard.rationale: An unblinded ground turmeric with naproxen comparison favored relief in dysmenorrhea and a formulated-curcumin clinical comparison provides a separate signal. Whole turmeric powder was inconclusive in hand osteoarthritis. The Cochrane pooled estimate was below the review's clinical threshold with unresolved member overlap. The Parkinson nanomicelle pilot did not report a separate pain item. New curcumin experiments concern restoration of thermal sensitivity after cisplatin in rats and a laryngeal amyloidosis case with prior pain-directed radiation and persistent arthritic pain. These supply exposure context. The earlier close culinary and formulated comparisons retain minimal easing. Direct culinary Parkinson pain evidence remains open. A separate kinase review traces experiments on curcumin to the turmeric constituent. Its signaling endpoints do not measure pain and supply no direct support or contradiction for ground turmeric. The additional sources distinguish a turmeric extract in a cellular screen, a branded formulation in brain-tumor cell lines and traditional topical cosmetic use in the Marquesas. They add no pain direction and preserve the lean from the closer culinary and non-Parkinson comparisons. The previously grouped rodent results are separated into their four underlying study families. The full formalin original distinguishes later-phase attenuation from an inconclusive early phase and unrelated rotarod results. Injected, oral and intrathecal constituents and a combined extract do not change the tier based on closer human pain comparisons. Gut-barrier reviews and a neural stem-cell study supply context without a distinct pain comparison. The lipoxygenase review distinguishes curcumin from synthetic analogues and discusses enzyme activity without an independent culinary pain comparison. The additional original evaluates isolated curcumin in spinal injury and measures locomotor recovery and pathology. It supplies no pain-specific result after ground turmeric. The complete new study tests isolated curcumin in endothelial cells. Its injury outcome says nothing about pain severity after consuming ground turmeric. The additional curcumin studies and reviews concern isolated compounds, hippocampal outcomes or neoplastic mechanisms. No corresponding pain comparison after ground turmeric in Parkinson disease was recovered.
